title: core/material
description: A material for the magnetic cores

type.description: The type of a magnetic material

material.description: The composition of a magnetic material
material.title: materialType

materialComposition.description: The composition of a magnetic material
materialComposition.title: materialComposition

alternatives.description: A list of alternative materials that could replace this one
alternatives.title: coreMaterialAlternatives

name.description: The name of a magnetic material

commercialName.description: The name of a magnetic material together its manufacturer

family.description: The family of a magnetic material according to its manufacturer

curieTemperature.description: The temperature at which this material loses all ferromagnetism. Unit: Celsius.

saturation.description: BH curve points characterising the saturation flux density of the material. By convention, saturation is reported at the field strength at which the relative differential permeability has fallen to approximately 10 % of the initial permeability. See docs/normative-references.md.

remanence.description: BH Cycle points where the magnetic field is 0

coerciveForce.description: BH Cycle points where the magnetic flux density is 0

heatConductivity.description: Thermal conductivity value according to manufacturer. Unit: W/(m*K).

heatCapacity.description: Specific heat capacity value according to manufacturer. Unit: J/(kg*K).

density.description: Density value according to manufacturer, in kg/m3

permeability.description: Relative permeability of the magnetic material, broken down by which kind of permeability was measured. At minimum `initial` is required for materials that have one (essentially all ferrites and tape-wound alloys). Each entry uses permeabilityPoint, which pins frequency, temperature, AC peak flux density and DC bias per measurement.
permeability.title: permeabilities

initial.description: Initial relative permeability mu_i. Measured at near-zero AC excitation (e.g. B < 0.25 mT) and low frequency (typically <= 10 kHz) at the material's reference temperature, per the IEC 60401-3 catalogue convention.

amplitude.description: Amplitude relative permeability mu_a. The secant slope of the BH curve at a specified peak AC flux density on a defined geometry. Each point pins B_peak, frequency and temperature.

incremental.description: Incremental relative permeability mu_delta. The slope of a small AC excursion superimposed on a non-zero DC bias H. Each point pins magneticFieldDcBias and the AC magneticFluxDensityPeak. Required to model inductors operating under DC bias (PFC chokes, output filters, flyback primaries).

reversible.description: Reversible relative permeability mu_rev. The limit of mu_delta as the AC excursion tends to zero. Tabulated vs magneticFieldDcBias; used for small-signal AC analysis around a DC operating point.

complex.description: Complex relative permeability (mu' + j*mu''), used for high-frequency loss modelling.
complex.title: complexPermeabilityData

permittivity.description: Relative permittivity of the material. Ferrites (MnZn grades in particular) have a very large, frequency-dependent permittivity that, together with the permeability, sets the in-material electromagnetic wavelength lambda = c / (f * sqrt(mu' * eps')) and therefore the onset of dimensional effects (dimensional resonance) and the effective usable bandwidth of a given core size. Optional; primarily relevant to high-frequency (MHz) modelling and to tools that account for displacement current.
permittivity.title: permittivities

complex.description: Complex relative permittivity (eps_r' - j*eps_r''), used for dimensional-effect and displacement-current modelling at high frequency.
complex.title: complexPermittivityData

volumetricLosses.description: Volumetric core losses. Values throughout this block are in watts per cubic metre (W/m^3). Coefficient-based methods (Steinmetz, Roshen, ...) assume the same unit system: P in W/m^3, f in Hz, B in T (peak). See docs/units.md and docs/normative-references.md.
volumetricLosses.title: volumetricLosses

additionalProperties.title: volumetricLossesMethodsData
additionalProperties.description: Object whose keys are the shape families for which these volumetric losses are valid. If the key is absent the variant applies to all shapes.

recommendations.description: Manufacturer recommended operating conditions for this material
recommendations.title: coreMaterialRecommendations

minimumFrequency.description: Minimum recommended operating frequency in Hz

maximumFrequency.description: Maximum recommended operating frequency in Hz

maximumMagneticFluxDensity.description: Maximum recommended AC flux density, in T

maximumOperatingTemperature.description: Maximum recommended operating temperature in Celsius

massLosses.description: Mass-specific core losses. Values throughout this block are in watts per kilogram (W/kg). Note: this is the per-mass form used for tape-wound, amorphous and nanocrystalline materials; the per-volume form lives in `volumetricLosses` and uses W/m^3. The two are NOT interchangeable without the material density. See docs/units.md and docs/normative-references.md.
massLosses.title: massLosses

additionalProperties.title: massLossesMethodsData
additionalProperties.description: Object whose keys are the shape families for which these mass losses are valid. If the key is absent the variant applies to all shapes.

permittivityPoint.title: permittivityPoint

temperature.description: temperature for the field value, in Celsius

frequency.description: Frequency of the electric field, in Hz

lossFactorCoreLossesMethodData.title: lossFactorCoreLossesMethodData

permeabilityPoint.title: permeabilityPoint

temperature.description: temperature for the field value, in Celsius

magneticFluxDensityPeak.description: magnetic flux density peak for the field value, in T

magneticFieldPeak.description: Peak magnetic field strength H of the measurement, in A/m. The H-side counterpart of magneticFluxDensityPeak: some manufacturers (e.g. Samwha) specify amplitude-permeability curves by peak H instead of peak B.

magneticFieldDcBias.description: DC bias in the magnetic field, in A/m

frequency.description: Frequency of the Magnetic field, in Hz

modifiers.description: Per-manufacturer factor blocks applied to the base permeability value to account for DC bias, frequency and temperature dependence.

additionalProperties.description: Object where keys are shape families for which this permeability is valid. If missing, the variant is valid for all shapes
additionalProperties.title: initialPermeabilitModifier

bhCyclePoint.description: One point of the BH cycle.

magneticFluxDensity.description: Magnetic flux density value. Unit: T.

magneticField.description: Magnetic field strength value. Unit: A/m.

temperature.description: Temperature for the field value, in Celsius.

steinmetzCoreLossesMethodData.description: Steinmetz coefficients for estimating volumetric losses in a given frequency range. The model is P = k * f^alpha * B^beta. By normative convention in MAS, P is in W/m^3, f in Hz and B in T (peak); k therefore has units of W/(m^3 * Hz^alpha * T^beta). Datasheets that publish coefficients in scaled units (kW/m^3, mW/cm^3, kHz, mT) must be converted before serialisation.
steinmetzCoreLossesMethodData.title: steinmetzCoreLossesMethodData

minimumFrequency.description: minimum frequency for which the coefficients are valid, in Hz

maximumFrequency.description: maximum frequency for which the coefficients are valid, in Hz

beta.description: magnetic flux density power coefficient beta

volumetricLossesPoint.description: data for describing the volumetric losses at a given point of magnetic flux density, frequency and temperature
volumetricLossesPoint.title: volumetricLossesPoint

origin.description: Origin of the data (datasheet, measurement, simulation, fitted).

massLossesPoint.description: Mass-specific losses at a given point of magnetic flux density, frequency and temperature. Unit: W/kg.

magneticsPermeabilityMethodData.title: magneticsPermeabilityMethodData

magneticFieldDcBiasFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the H DC bias, as factor = a + b * pow(H, c)

frequencyFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the frequency, as factor = a + b * f + c * pow(f, 2) + d * pow(f, 3) + e * pow(f, 4)

temperatureFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the temperature, as factor = a + b * T + c * pow(T, 2) + d * pow(T, 3) + e * pow(T, 4)

micrometalsPermeabilityMethodData.description: Coefficients given by Micrometals in order to calculate the permeability of their cores
micrometalsPermeabilityMethodData.title: micrometalsPermeabilityMethodData

magneticFieldDcBiasFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the H DC bias, as factor = a + b * pow(H, c) + d

magneticFluxDensityFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the B field, as factor = = 1 / ( 1 / ( a + b * pow(B,c)) + 1 / (d * pow(B, e) ) + 1 / f )

frequencyFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the frequency, as factor = 1 / (a + b * pow(f, c) ) + d

temperatureFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the temperature, as either factor = a * (T -20) * 0.0001 or factor = (a + c * T + e * pow(T, 2)) / (1 + b * T + d * pow(T, 2))

fairRitePermeabilityMethodData.description: Coefficients given by Fair-Rite in order to calculate the permeability of their materials
fairRitePermeabilityMethodData.title: fairRitePermeabilityMethodData

temperatureFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the temperature, as either factor = a

pocoPermeabilityMethodData.description: Coefficients given by Poco in order to calculate the permeability of their materials
pocoPermeabilityMethodData.title: pocoPermeabilityMethodData

magneticFieldDcBiasFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the H DC bias, as factor = a + b * pow(H, c) + d

frequencyFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with frequency, as the percent-of-initial rolloff factor = (a / (1 + pow(f / b, c)) + d) * 0.01, with f in Hz. a is the rolling-off share, d the high-frequency asymptote (a + d = 100 at DC), b the corner frequency in Hz and c the steepness. Fitted to the permeability-vs-frequency curves of the POCO catalog.

tdgPermeabilityMethodData.description: Coefficients given by TDG in order to calculate the permeability of their materials
tdgPermeabilityMethodData.title: tdgPermeabilityMethodData

magneticFieldDcBiasFactor.description: Field with the coefficients used to calculate how much the permeability decreases with the H DC bias, as factor = 1 / (a + b * pow(H, c))
